_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); defense prime contractor signals

pit_profile.why: 'In 2013, 82% of our $45.4 billion in net sales were from the U.S. Government, either as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor (including 61% from the Department of Defense (DoD))' (FY2013 10-K, Item 1); 'We depend heavily on contracts with the U.S. Government. ... Those contracts are conditioned upon the continuing availability of Congressional appropriations.' (Item 1A): sales that depend on Congressional appropriations are not earnings that are the cycle, so DURABLE (the CAT and SO precedent); OFFSHORE (live from 2004-11-05) is scoped to offshore delivery taking share in Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing, and CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) to public cloud displacing on-premise hardware, storage, databases and data-center outsourcing; the 10-K names no offshore competition and does not mention cloud, so no disruption theme in scope is live

classification.quality_note: 'In 2013, 82% of our $45.4 billion in net sales were from the U.S. Government, either as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor (including 61% from the Department of Defense (DoD))' (FY2013 10-K, Item 1); 'We depend heavily on contracts with the U.S. Government. ... Those contracts are conditioned upon the continuing availability of Congressional appropriations.' (Item 1A): sales that depend on Congressional appropriations are not earnings that are the cycle, so DURABLE (the CAT and SO precedent); OFFSHORE (live from 2004-11-05) is scoped to offshore delivery taking share in Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing, and CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) to public cloud displacing on-premise hardware, storage, databases and data-center outsourcing; the 10-K names no offshore competition and does not mention cloud, so no disruption theme in scope is live. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 2.15x; +74% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.04; conservative 2yr -16%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -6.9%/yr (worst year FY04-FY13, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +2.2%/yr (FY14 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.8%/yr (FY04-FY13 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +42.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY04-FY13); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: LMT (retrospective, 2014-03-14) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.15x (45.8% downside to Bear $88 / +21.3% upside to Bull $197) | Adj composite 1.95 vs market 2.99: gap -1.04 [OVERVALUED] | +74% above the EPP floor $94 (9x FY14E $10.40) | Conservative 2-yr case: -16.1% total (-8.1%/yr) | At 15.6x FY14E the 15% hurdle price $215 sits above the BULL case; backlog +0.4% in Q4 2013, forward revenues -3% to +0.3% (FY14 net sales guide); OFFSHORE (live from 2004-11-05) is scoped to offshore delivery in Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing, and CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) to public cloud displacing on-premise hardware, storage, databases and data-center outsourcing; the 10-Ks name no offshore competition and do not mention cloud, so no theme in scope has dated evidence.
